profile.name: Sumit Sinha
profile.tagline: I build production real-time systems and multi-tenant SaaS.
profile.summary: Full Stack Engineer with 2.5+ years building production real-time systems and multi-tenant SaaS — Node.js, NestJS, React, PostgreSQL, WebRTC.
about: I'm a full stack engineer working across the whole path a feature takes — from a Postgres schema and a NestJS service to the React screen someone actually clicks. Most of what I've shipped lives in the awkward middle: real-time systems, multi-tenant data, and the plumbing that keeps both honest.

At 8byte.ai I build a multi-tenant CRM that runs loan workflows for several NBFC brands off one codebase — role-based access, customer segmentation, and a WhatsApp Business API integration that replaced manual follow-ups across a nine-step onboarding flow.

Before that, at Videosdk.live, I built a collaborative whiteboard on WebRTC + MediaSoup for a video conferencing platform. When WebSocket drawing events started dragging production down, I split presence and drawing into multiplexed channels to keep it stable until we migrated to tldraw.
Between roles I don't idle. StreamHub and ClearLoop both came out of those gaps — production-grade, deployed, and built under real constraints instead of tutorial ones.
profile.aboutHeading: Half systems engineer. Half product brain.
profile.aboutSub: Comfortable in the query plan and in the design review.

points: Built multi-tenant CRM using NestJS and Next.js, enabling loan management workflows across multiple NBFC brands through centralized role-based access control and customer segmentation
Integrated WhatsApp Business API via AiSensy to automate loan journey notifications across a 9-step onboarding flow, replacing manual follow-ups with automated status updates
Developed customer support chatbot and lead lifecycle logging system tracking key events across the loan application journey
Built production collaborative whiteboard using WebRTC, WebSockets, and MediaSoup for a video conferencing platform, supporting real-time multi-user drawing and annotations

Developed and maintained product pages, technical blogs, and website content using Strapi as a headless CMS, enabling non-technical teams to manage content while integrating seamlessly with the React frontend

When WebSocket-based drawing events caused production lag, proposed and implemented connection multiplexing to separate presence and drawing channels — kept the feature stable until migration to tldraw
Created AI agent workflow system using React Flow enabling automated meeting configuration
Developed frontend components and REST APIs using React.js and Node.js for client projects
Developed 3 production applications using React, TypeScript, and Elasticsearch including ML-powered chatbot and AI-based conference recommendation system

projects.title: StreamHub
projects.subtitle: Live Video Broadcasting Platform
projects.description: MediaSoup SFU-based WebRTC platform for real-time video broadcasting and screen sharing with system audio. The interesting part was the VOD pipeline: the whole thing runs on a 1GB RAM server, so recording goes out as MediaRecorder chunked uploads to Cloudflare R2, with FFmpeg processing pushed async through RabbitMQ and results cached in Redis.
highlights: Constraint-driven VOD pipeline designed for a 1GB RAM server
MediaRecorder chunked uploads to Cloudflare R2, async FFmpeg via RabbitMQ
Backend on Oracle Cloud with PM2, frontend on Vercel

projects.title: ClearLoop
projects.subtitle: Engineering Context Layer
projects.description: Multi-tenant SaaS that pulls GitHub PRs, features, bugs and release notes into one context layer for engineering teams. Shared-schema PostgreSQL with tenant isolation, plus a GitHub App whose webhooks link PRs to features automatically and generate release notes from what actually merged.
highlights: Shared-schema PostgreSQL with row-level tenant isolation
GitHub App webhooks for automatic PR-to-feature linking
Auto-generated release notes from merged work
